presentingComplaint: Several weeks of progressive fatigue, exertional breathlessness and light-headedness.
history: 58-year-old woman with 6-8 weeks of worsening tiredness, dyspnoea on climbing one flight of stairs, palpitations and near-syncope on standing. Reports heavy, prolonged menstrual periods for over a year and long-standing NSAID use for osteoarthritis. Occasional black stools noted in the past month. No overt haematemesis. Poor dietary iron intake, no known bleeding disorder. No fever, night sweats or significant weight loss.
examination: Marked conjunctival and palmar pallor, koilonychia and angular cheilitis. Resting tachycardia with a soft ejection systolic flow murmur at the left sternal edge. No lymphadenopathy, no hepatosplenomegaly, no petechiae or bruising. Chest clear; mild ankle oedema. PR examination: melaena on the glove, no mass.

labs.peripheral smear: microcytic hypochromic RBCs, anisopoikilocytosis, pencil cells

imaging: Chest X-ray normal; no acute cardiopulmonary process. Upper and lower GI endoscopy planned to localise chronic blood loss.
differentialDiagnoses: Iron-deficiency anaemia from chronic GI/menstrual blood loss
Occult GI malignancy causing blood loss
finalDiagnosis: Symptomatic iron-deficiency anaemia due to chronic blood loss
citations: Harrison 22e — Iron Deficiency and Other Hypoproliferative Anemias
AABB/ICMR Red Cell Transfusion Thresholds (restrictive strategy) 2016
contraindications: Avoid unnecessary transfusion in a haemodynamically compensated patient — use restrictive threshold (Hb <7 g/dL, or <8 g/dL if cardiac disease/symptomatic)
Oral iron GI intolerance; consider IV iron if malabsorption or intolerance
Do not start iron before samples for ferritin/iron studies drawn
edgeCases: Coexisting anaemia of chronic disease can raise ferritin into the 'normal' range and mask iron deficiency — low transferrin saturation still suggests deficiency
In a postmenopausal woman or any man, iron deficiency must be assumed to be GI blood loss (occult malignancy) until proven otherwise by endoscopy
expectedMaiK: This is symptomatic iron-deficiency anaemia (microcytic, hypochromic, low ferritin, low transferrin saturation) driven by chronic blood loss; the priority is to determine the transfusion threshold based on symptoms/cardiac reserve and to localise the bleeding source, not to treat empirically as infection.
expectedNextQuestions: Any overt or occult GI blood loss (melaena, haematochezia, dyspepsia, NSAID use)?
Menstrual and obstetric history / postmenopausal status?
Dietary iron intake and features of malabsorption (coeliac symptoms)?
expectedInvestigations: Iron studies (ferritin, serum iron, TIBC, transferrin saturation)
Peripheral blood smear and reticulocyte count
Upper and lower GI endoscopy to localise chronic blood loss
regressionAssertions: differential must not include any infective/sepsis id
